about: Neutral carbon (C I) data for the Carbon mode, issue #144 Phase 1. See docs/research/carbon-atom.md. Built by scripts/research/carbon_data.py.

accuracy_codes.note: upper bound of the relative uncertainty of A, E is over 0.50

asd.cite: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J., and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12). National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. DOI 10.18434/T4W30F

hk2017.cite: K. Haris and A. Kramida, Critically evaluated spectral data for neutral carbon (C I), Astrophys. J. Suppl. Ser. 233, 16 (2017), DOI 10.3847/1538-4365/aa86ab, arXiv:1704.07474

mchf.cite: NIST MCHF/MCDHF Collection, version 2 (C. Froese Fischer, G. Tachiev), C I energy levels and lifetimes, Breit-Pauli. Its reference list (references.pl) returned HTTP 500, so the paper behind the table is not named here

bunge1993.cite: C. F. Bunge, J. A. Barrientos and A. V. Bunge, Roothaan-Hartree-Fock ground-state atomic wave functions: Slater-type orbital expansions and expectation values for Z = 2-54, At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 53, 113 (1993), file RHF.TABLES as mirrored by the Computational Chemistry List

cie1931.cite: CIE (2019), Colour-matching functions of CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer (data table, 1 nm, from CIE 018:2019 Table 6), International Commission on Illumination, Vienna, DOI 10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b

css4.cite: W3C, CSS Color Module Level 4, Candidate Recommendation Draft of 2026-10-09, section 19, XYZ_to_lin_sRGB and gam_sRGB

outer_electron.note: n* = sqrt(R_C / (limit centroid - term centroid)), centroids g-weighted, computed here from asd levels. Model orbital P(r) = N r^(lambda+1) exp(-r/n*) L_{n_r}^{(2 lambda + 1)}(2 r / n*), lambda = n* - n_r - 1, mean_r = (3 n*^2 - lambda (lambda + 1)) / 2

ground_rhf.form: R_nl(r) = sum_j c_j N_j r^(n_j - 1) exp(-zeta_j r), N_j = (2 zeta_j)^(n_j + 1/2) / sqrt((2 n_j)!), r in bohr

angular.note: density of a subshell = sum_m n_m |Y_lm|^2 R(r)^2. spin and M_S do not enter. Occupations from Clebsch-Gordan coefficients (sympy)
